import random
from typing import List, Tuple

def policy(board: List[List[int]]) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """
    Battleship AI policy.

    It first checks for any hits on the opponent's board. If hits exist,
    it builds a set of candidate cells that are directly adjacent (Manhattan distance <=2)
    to at least one hit and that lie in the same row/column gap or at the ends of a
    horizontal/vertical cluster. Candidates are scored by the number of hits in their
    immediate neighbourhood. The highest‑scoring candidates are returned, with random
    tie‑breaking to make the policy less exploitable.

    If there are no hits (or no candidates), the policy falls back to a
    deterministic scanning of the remaining unknown cells. The scan proceeds in a
    left‑to‑right, top‑to‑bottom order and remembers the last guessed cell so that
    subsequent scans continue where it left off.

    The implementation keeps persistent state across calls through the function
    object, so the history of previous shots is retained without having to receive
    any additional arguments.
    """
    # Persistent state stored as function attributes
    if not hasattr(policy, "_last_scanned"):
        policy._last_scanned = (-1, -1)
    last_scanned = policy._last_scanned  # tuple of ints

    # Identify hits and unknown cells on the current board
    hits = [(r, c) for r in range(10) for c in range(10) if board[r][c] == 1]
    unknown_cells = [(r, c) for r in range(10) for c in range(10) if board[r][c] == 0]

    # 1. Hit‑expansion phase
